newsitem.title: USA: Perot says debate shut-out would spell doom.
newsitem.headline: Perot says debate shut-out would spell doom.

text.p: Ross Perot, speaking in the city originally scheduled to host the first presidential election debate on Wednesday, said his third party effort was doomed if he could not participate in the debates between President Bill Clinton and Bob Dole.
"We can't possibly win if we're not in those debates," Perot told a largely student audience at St. Louis University. "We've got to get in the game and we will."

The Commission on Presidential Debates last week recommended excluding Reform Party candidate Perot and his running mate, Pat Choate, saying they did not have a realistic chance of winning the election. Debates were scheduled next month between Clinton and Dole in Hartford, Connecticut and San Diego.

Under the tentative schedule of debates drafted earlier in the election year, the first face-off was to have been Wednesday evening at Washington University in St. Louis, the venue for the first debate in 1992 in which Perot took part.
Perot called the commission a corrupt organisation consisting of major party members. He said he hoped legal action he had taken would allow him to be included in the coming Clinton-Dole face-offs.
Perot captured 19 percent of the vote in the 1992 presidential election but polls this year indicate his support is about a third of that.
